theShortAnswer: The two packets are page-text identical because BOTH correctly refuse every election on CR-65, and they refuse DIFFERENT sections of it. al-felony-nonconviction-90-set owes a disjunctive election in Section III; al-pardoned-felony-set owes a conjunctive sworn certification in Section V. Neither section can be ticked from what the platform holds, so both render blank, and blank equals blank. Identity here is the consequence of two correct refusals, not a defect of either. What was genuinely wrong is that neither packet said WHICH section was its own on the paper, and one of the two guides omitted three elections CR-65 makes every petitioner make.

separateUnresolvedLegalQuestion.question: Whether 'any felony offense' survived the most recent amendments to § 15-27-2(a), given that the archive and the internal reference both carry the older non-violent framing.
separateUnresolvedLegalQuestion.whatTheHeldSourceShows: CR-65 Rev. 10/2024 Section III prints no non-violence qualifier anywhere in its lead-in or in any of its eight options. The AOC handles violent felonies separately, in Section IV, and only as CONVICTIONS within the trafficking exception. The form revision post-dates the track's effectiveFrom of 2024-10-01.
separateUnresolvedLegalQuestion.whatThatDoesAndDoesNotSettle: It removes the stated basis for the doubt -- the older non-violent framing is not what the current official petition prints. It does not read § 15-27-2(a) itself, which AL.memo.json separately records as never having been read. A form is evidence of the AOC's reading of the statute; it is not the statute.
separateUnresolvedLegalQuestion.proposedNarrowFix: Acquire the current official § 15-27-2(a) text from alison.legislature.state.al.us and compare. That is source acquisition, not a legal call, and it is already the memo's own second unresolvedQuestion for this track.

disputedInterpretation.memoEntry: AL-7, unresolvedQuestions[0], impact build_blocker, affectedElement eligibility_branch
disputedInterpretation.question: Whether a pardon that expressly withholds firearm rights satisfies the statutory requirement of restoration of civil and political rights. Alabama pardons are commonly granted with restrictions, and after State ex rel. Sokira v. Burr the Board commonly excludes firearm rights expressly.
disputedInterpretation.whyItIsDispositiveAndNotClerical: Check Box10.6 asks the petitioner to swear to a certificate of pardon WITH RESTORATION of civil and political rights; Check Box11.0 asks them to swear that all forfeited civil and political rights HAVE BEEN RESTORED. If a firearms carve-out defeats restoration, this route does not fit the participant at all and the correct output is a refusal, not a petition. The same memo carries it as a selfHelpStopCondition: 'The pardon withholds firearm rights and the restoration question controls.'

searchForAnAlreadyAdoptedDecision.scopeSearched: All 15 files in data/record-clearing/legal-decisions/, plus route-ratification-registry.json.
searchForAnAlreadyAdoptedDecision.evidence: 2026-08-28-national-legal-decisions.json carries 35 questionDecisions. Not one has jurisdiction AL. Alabama appears in that overlay only in researchTrackDecisions, for al-olr and al-uncharged-arrest. No file mentions al-pardoned-felony, 15-27-2, or AL-7.

nearestAdoptedDecision.holding: Treat the pardon route as available only when the operative clemency instrument expressly grants a full pardon of the conviction sought to be expunged. A commutation, reprieve, remission of fine, restoration of civil rights, or partial/conditional grant is not the same legal instrument. An ambiguous document should not be characterized by participant attestation alone.
nearestAdoptedDecision.whyItDoesNotDecideAL7: It is keyed to a Kentucky track and answers a different question -- is this instrument a full pardon -- where AL-7 asks whether a full pardon carrying a firearms carve-out satisfies Alabama's statutory restoration requirement. Jurisdiction membership grants nothing and a route sells only what a record keyed to it proves.
nearestAdoptedDecision.whyItStillMatters: Its adopted product rule -- do not characterise the instrument from attestation, route conditional or ambiguous grants to counsel -- is the shape this packet already takes. The pardoned-felony packet ticks nothing, hands the certificate reading back to the participant, and carries the firearm stop condition verbatim. So the packet's current behaviour needs no repair on that limb; only the eligibility branch behind it needs a decision.
